title: Where functions start
description:
Find likely function starts in x64 code from common prologues.

```
0x0000  48 89 5C 24 08   mov [rsp+8], rbx     (prologue)
0x0010  40 53            push rbx             (prologue)
0x0020  48 83 EC 28      sub rsp, 0x28        (prologue)
3 candidates; 0xCC padding between them
```
hints: Store each pattern as a `std::vector<int>` with -1 meaning "any byte", so `48 83 EC xx` is `{ 0x48, 0x83, 0xEC, -1 }`; the prologues themselves are in lesson 2.02.
Real tools use the exception directory (`.pdata`), which lists every function's start exactly; this guesser is a fallback.
requirements: Search for a few byte patterns from lesson 2.02 (`48 83 EC xx`, `40 53`, `48 89 5C 24 08`, `55 48 8B EC`).
A candidate counts more when it follows `C3` (ret) or `CC` padding.
Print each with its pattern's meaning. Use code from a program you compiled.
stretch: Read the `.pdata` entries (start RVA, end RVA, unwind info) from a PE file instead.
